title: Cartoon Network
wiki_lead:
Cartoon Network (CN) is an American cable television network and the flagship property of The Cartoon Network, Inc., a corporate umbrella within the television division of Skydance. Launched on October 1, 1992, it primarily broadcasts animated television series, mostly children's programming, ranging from action to animated comedy. 
It currently runs from 6 a.m. to 5 p.m. ET/PT daily and primarily targets children aged 6 to 12, though some early morning programming, formerly of the Cartoonito block, is aimed at preschool-aged children, while evening block Adult Swim targets young adults. 
It was brought under common ownership with long-time rival Nickelodeon following the 2026 acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by the parent company of Nickelodeon, Paramount Skydance (now known as Skydance).
As of November 2023, Cartoon Network is available to approximately 66 million pay television households in the United States — down from its peak of 100 million households in 2011.

History

On August 9, 1986, Turner Broadcasting System acquired Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer/United Artists (MGM/UA). On October 18, Turner forcibly sold back MGM. However, Turner kept much of the film and television library made before May 1986 (including some of the UA library) and formed Turner Entertainment Co. On October 8, 1988, its cable channel Turner Network Television (TNT) was launched and gained an audience with its extensive film library. In 1991, Turner also purchased the library of animation studio Hanna-Barbera. Ted Turner selected Betty Cohen (then-Senior Vice President of TNT) to devise a network to house these programs. On February 18, 1992, Turner Broadcasting announced its plans to launch Cartoon Network as an outlet for an animation library. On March 12, 1992, its namesake corporate parent company was founded one month after Turner's plan was announced. On October 1, 1992, the network officially launched as the first 24-hour single-genre cable channel with animation as its main theme. Betty Cohen was appointed as its first president.

In 1994, Hanna-Barbera's new division Cartoon Network Studios was founded and started production on What a Cartoon!. This show debuted in 1995, offering original animated shorts. In 1996, Cartoon Network aired two preschool programs: Big Bag, a live-action/puppet television program with animated short series produced by Children's Television Workshop, and Small World, which featured animated series aimed at preschoolers imported from foreign countries. Turner Broadcasting System merged with Time Warner, which consolidated/reverted ownership of all the Warner Bros. cartoons. The network could then continue more original productions.

grok_lead: Cartoon Network is an American basic cable and satellite television channel owned by Warner Bros. Discovery that specializes in animated programming for children, preteens, and young adults. Launched on October 1, 1992, by the Turner Broadcasting System under the direction of Betty Cohen, it became the world's first 24-hour network dedicated exclusively to animation, initially airing classic cartoons from the Turner library such as those by Hanna-Barbera. The channel quickly achieved high viewership, ranking number one among basic cable networks in time spent viewing by January 1993. Over its history, Cartoon Network expanded into original programming through initiatives like What a Cartoon!, which incubated acclaimed series including Dexter's Laboratory (1996), Johnny Bravo (1997), and The Powerpuff Girls (1998), establishing it as a hub for innovative animation that earned multiple Emmy Awards and global popularity. In 2001, it introduced the late-night block Adult Swim, targeting older audiences with edgier content like Space Ghost Coast to Coast and later Rick and Morty, diversifying its appeal amid industry shifts toward streaming. While celebrated for revitalizing hand-drawn animation in the 1990s and 2000s, the network has faced challenges including declining linear TV ratings due to cord-cutting and competition from digital platforms, prompting layoffs and a pivot to shorter-form shows like Teen Titans Go! starting in 2013.
